cards.text: Jeremiah the prophet is still writing his letter to the exiles carried off to Babylon. He sees it coming: some of them may say the LORD has raised up prophets for them right there in Babylon. So he answers the comments before anybody even posts them.
Then the LORD speaks about the king who sits on David's throne and all the people still in Jerusalem, their brothers who didn't go into exile. Brace yourself, friend.

cards.question: What will the LORD of Hosts send against the king and the people still in Jerusalem?

cards.text: He'll make them like rotten figs, so bad they cannot be eaten. He'll make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth, a curse and an object of scorn among the nations where He banishes them.

cards.question: Why will the LORD do all this to the people still in Jerusalem?

answers.text: They have not listened to His words
They refused to pay tribute to Babylon
They tore down the altar in the temple

cards.question: Again and again, the LORD sent His words to the people in Jerusalem through His servants the ___.
Unlike the people in Jerusalem, the exiles in Babylon have listened to the LORD's words.

cards.text: Now the LORD turns to the exiles and names names: Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, two men prophesying lies to them in His name. Not "some folks are saying," friend. First names AND their fathers' names.

cards.question: The LORD will deliver Ahab and Zedekiah to ___ king of Babylon.
Ahab and Zedekiah will be killed somewhere far away, out of the exiles' sight.

cards.text: Their names become a curse among the exiles of Judah in Babylon: "May the LORD make you like Zedekiah and Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire!"

cards.question: Besides lying in the LORD's name, what outrage does the LORD say Ahab and Zedekiah committed?
The LORD says He knows what Ahab and Zedekiah did, and He is a witness.

cards.text: Next comes a message for Shemaiah the Nehelamite, a man who's been working the mail like it's his second job. He's sent letters to all the people of Jerusalem, to Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest, and to all the priests.

cards.question: Shemaiah sent letters to the people of Jerusalem and the priests. Whose name did he send them in?

cards.text: Shemaiah tells Zephaniah the LORD has appointed him priest in place of Jehoiada, to be chief officer in the house of the LORD. And that job, Shemaiah says, includes any madman who acts like a prophet.

cards.question: Shemaiah tells Zephaniah that a madman who acts like a prophet must be put in stocks and neck irons.

cards.text: Then Shemaiah gets to his point, and friend, the point has a name on it. He wants to know why Zephaniah hasn't rebuked a certain man from Anathoth who, Shemaiah says, poses as a prophet.

cards.question: Shemaiah asks Zephaniah why he hasn't rebuked ___ of Anathoth.
Shemaiah complains that Jeremiah told the exiles in Babylon: since the exile will be ___, build houses and settle down.
Zephaniah the priest gets Shemaiah's letter. What does he do with it?

cards.text: Shemaiah's letter about Jeremiah gets read to Jeremiah. That's emailing your boss to complain about a coworker, and your boss reads it to the coworker OUT LOUD.
Then the word of the LORD comes to Jeremiah: send all the exiles a message about Shemaiah the Nehelamite. A message about a letter about a letter, friend, and my head's spinning like a mixer on high.

cards.question: The LORD says He sent Shemaiah to prophesy to the exiles.
What does the LORD say Shemaiah has made the exiles do?
The LORD will punish Shemaiah and his ___, and Shemaiah will not see the ___ the LORD will bring to His people.
Why does the LORD say He will punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite?

answers.text: He preached rebellion against the LORD
He stole from the house of the LORD
He bowed to the idols of Babylon

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "Now the LORD turns to the exiles... in His name." / "Not 'some folks are saying,' friend." / "First names AND their fathers' names." Only the opening card may run to 3 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card only restates verses 17-18 (rotten figs, horror, curse, scorn) with no reaction, comparison or storyteller line, so it reads like a plain summary instead of Papa Dorin telling it.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Shemaiah the Nehelamite appears here for the first time, but the card only jokes about his letter-writing and never says simply who he is. It doesn't say that he is one of the exiles writing from Babylon (29:28, 29:31). Without that, the baker doesn't know where his letters are coming from or why they matter.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This card retells 29:29, which the choice card right before it (card 8) just asked about and answered. It doesn't move the passage forward. It recaps that answer so a joke can ride on it. The joke should ride on a card that carries the next piece of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.
